Right = A

Code examples (apply the same rule to any A/B code)
- A1 — hit the right-side target 1 time. (CONFIRMED_LIVE)

- B2 — hit the left-side target 2 times. (CONFIRMED_LIVE)

- A3 / B3 — same counting rule: A3 = hit right target 3 times, B3 = hit left target 3 times. (CONFIRMED_LIVE)

Step-by-step: solve the hanging-target room
1. Enter the room and listen/read the speaker code (letter + number). (CONFIRMED_LIVE)
2. Map the letter to a side: A → right target, B → left target. (CONFIRMED_LIVE)
3. Apply the number as the exact count of hits to that side (e.g., B2 = two hits on left). (CONFIRMED_LIVE)
4. Use fast/light attacks to register hits cleanly — these were the safest observed inputs during the current EA window. (CONFIRMED_LIVE)
5. After landing the indicated hits, check for the puzzle’s response. If it reports Incorrect, proceed to the troubleshooting section below before repeating attempts.

- This is a player-reported observation only — not an officially confirmed bug. If you have Four Arms equipped and the puzzle behaves unexpectedly, try unequipping the talisman and retesting the puzzle. (PLAYER_REPORTED)

If this didn't work
- Reload the area or exit/re-enter the room and try again; retrying is the recommended immediate step if the puzzle does not register correctly. (CONFIRMED_LIVE)
- Remember Withering Realms is in Early Access; puzzle behavior can be patch-sensitive. The observations above were made during the 2026-09-04 Early Access window and checked on 2026-09-07. If problems persist, watch official patch notes for changes. (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL / CONFIRMED_LIVE)

body.intro: Not a fixed numeric password — Bellflower Occult Institute hex doors use Spell Book Codes (book)-(word) pairs. Read the Spell Book Codes note for the door you want to open, collect the three books (Book of RAUM, Book of GLASYA-LABOLAS, Book of ASTAROTH), then at the hex door choose the book (prompt: “Speak words from which book?”) and speak the numbered word (prompt: “Speak which word?”) in the note’s pair order. Always use your own Spell Book Codes note — example words shown elsewhere are worked examples, not a universal password.

paragraphs: Not a fixed numeric password — Bellflower Occult Institute hex doors use Spell Book Codes (book)-(word) pairs. Read the Spell Book Codes note for the door you want to open, collect the three books (Book of RAUM, Book of GLASYA-LABOLAS, Book of ASTAROTH), then at the hex door choose the book (prompt: “Speak words from which book?”) and speak the numbered word (prompt: “Speak which word?”) in the note’s pair order. sections.title: Read Your Spell Book Codes Note
paragraphs: The clue note is printed with two labeled sets of (book)-(word) pairs: one labeled Basement and one labeled Upper floor. The note text in the observed run also says “The code is in book-word order.” Treat the pairs as ordered steps you must reproduce at the door that matches that label.
(Observed: in the recorded Early Access run the first two books referenced by the note were found in the ground-floor bathroom and the third book on the upper floor — CONFIRMED_LIVE.)

sections.title: Collect the Three Spell Books
paragraphs: You need all three books the note references. The three observed books are:

- Book of RAUM  
- Book of GLASYA-LABOLAS  
- Book of ASTAROTH

Each book contains a numbered list of words; the book tooltip reads: “A book of words that can be spoken aloud to dispel certain door hexes.” Locate the three books in your run and open each to read its numbered words before attempting the door.
(These three books and their word lists were documented in the observed run — CONFIRMED_LIVE.)

sections.title: How the Hex Door UI Works
paragraphs: When you interact with a hex door you get a two-step spoken-word UI:

- “Speak words from which book?” — pick one of the three books.  
- “Speak which word?” — pick the numbered word from that book.

If you select the wrong sequence the game responds with Clover saying “Nothin”; the correct sequence clears the door’s three glowing white sigils and opens the door (observed in the upper-floor door in the recorded run).

sections.title: Map Pairs to Words and Speak Them
paragraphs: Follow these steps in order for the door you are opening:

1. Open your Spell Book Codes note and find the pair list labeled for the door (Basement or Upper floor). Treat the list as ordered—first pair = first spoken book/word, etc.  
2. For the first pair: note the book index and the word index (format: book–word). Open that book, select it at the door when prompted (“Speak words from which book?”).  
3. When the door asks “Speak which word?”, choose the numbered word from that book (the list inside the book; 1 = first word, 2 = second, etc.). Speak it.  
4. Repeat for the second and third pairs in the note’s order. The correct three book-word selections in order will clear the sigils; a wrong selection yields “Nothin.”  
5. Use the pair set that matches the specific door (Basement vs Upper floor). Trying the other door’s pair list will not open this door in the observed run.
Important: use the Spell Book Codes note you found in your own playthrough — do not assume another player’s words will match your game.

sections.title: Worked Example From One Early Access Run
paragraphs: Below are worked mappings from one Early Access run (recorded stream). These are examples only — map pairs the same way using your own Spell Book Codes note.

Observed printed pairs in that run:
- Basement: 1-4  2-5  1-6  
- Upper floor: 1-6  2-4  3-2  (CONFIRMED_LIVE)
Mapped words from that same run:

- Upper floor mapping (example):  
  Sequence: 1-6 → 2-4 → 3-2  
  Mapped words: Book of RAUM / Azacgessenio → Book of GLASYA-LABOLAS / Manichel → Book of ASTAROTH / Hazalat  
  This sequence is shown opening the upper-floor hex door in the observed run.

- Basement mapping (example from the same run):  
  Sequence: 1-4 → 2-5 → 1-6  
  Mapped words: Book of RAUM / Sabanche → Book of GLASYA-LABOLAS / Saluyel → Book of RAUM / Azacgessenio  
  (Basement success frame for this run was not captured in the available clip; this mapping is the derived example from the note + books in that run — CONFIRMED_LIVE as the run’s mapping.)

Reminder: these word strings (Sabanche, Saluyel, Azacgessenio, Manichel, Hazalat, etc.) are worked examples from one run’s Spell Book Codes note. If your note lists different pairs, map them the same way to your three books.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
paragraphs:
- Using another player’s example words as if they’re universal — the correct words come from your own Spell Book Codes note.  
- Treating the UI as a digits-only keypad or expecting a single four-digit code — the game asks for a book then a word, not a numeric password.  
- Trying the Upper-floor pairs on the Basement door (or vice versa) — doors use their matching pair set in the observed run.  
- Picking the book but reading the wrong numbered word (remember 1 = first word in that book, etc.).  
- Skipping the third pair: all three pairs must be spoken in order to clear the door.
Also note: wrong sequences return Clover saying “Nothin”; correct sequences visibly clear the door’s sigils (CONFIRMED_LIVE).

sections.title: FAQ
paragraphs:
Q: Is there one password that works for everyone?  
A: No. There is not a universal password — doors use Spell Book Codes pairs from the note you find in your run.

Q: How do I read a pair like “1-6”?  
A: Read it as (book index)-(word index). Open the referenced book, then speak that numbered word (1 = first word, 6 = sixth word).

Q: What does the hex door ask me to do?  
A: The door asks “Speak words from which book?” then “Speak which word?” — choose the book, then choose the numbered word.

Q: Someone else’s words opened their door but not mine — why?  
A: Because each run’s Spell Book Codes note provides the pairs you must map to your three books. Using another player’s pairs may not match your note.

sections.title: Step-by-step progression
paragraphs:
1. Defeat the Chain Giant.  
   - The cemetery encounter shows the enemy name on the HUD as "Chain Giant."  
   - 
2. Claim the Ichorised Chain reward.  
   - After the fight the encounter reward popup reads exactly: "You found... Ichorised Chain" (a Crafting Material). The on-screen tooltip description: "A rare length of chain unearthed deep within a mine. Having been saturated in ichor for many years, it is remarkably strong and light." / "In the right hands, several powerful tools could be fashioned from it."  
   - 
3. Bring the Ichorised Chain to Rakesh (the Doll craftsman).  
   - The NPC is identified on the dialogue/UI as Rakesh; dialogue shown: "So, you have found a length of Ichorised Chain." Deliver the chain to him at his workbench.  
   - 
4. Receive the Chain Hook (Doll Left Hand).  
   - Rakesh provides the finished traversal tool named "Chain Hook" for £1. The Chain Hook tooltip text on-screen reads: "A length of ichorised chain tipped with a weighted dagger. Can be cast into wooden pilings to cross pits, or into enemies to close the distance quickly." Controls and stats shown in the same UI: "+Left Trigger Throw hook (Dexterity/Precision)"; 5 physical | 15 poise; 8 stamina toll.  
   - 
5. Use the Chain Hook at blocked gaps / pits.  
   - The Chain Hook’s on-screen description states it can be cast into wooden pilings to cross pits. The preservation of the progression chain is: defeat cemetery creature → claim Ichorised Chain → take to Rakesh → receive Chain Hook → use tool to cross blocked gaps.  
   -  (MISSING) — a direct in-VOD clip showing the player actually swinging across the gap was not captured in the available footage; the tool’s tooltip is the source for its pit-crossing function.

sections.title: Naming note — grappling hook → Chain Hook
paragraphs: - Public search queries for a "grappling hook" or "hook shot" should be mapped to the official in-game tool name: Chain Hook. The streamer used vernacular like "hook shot" or "grappling-hook-like tool," but the verified, on-screen name is Chain Hook and the chain item is spelled Ichorised Chain. Do not treat "grappling hook" as a separate official item name.

sections.title: If This Didn't Work
paragraphs: - Missing reward: If the Ichorised Chain does not appear after the cemetery fight, confirm the encounter completed. If still missing, this has been reported as a possible progression issue across builds and may need further verification from patch notes or support.

- Cannot trade/craft: If Rakesh will not accept the chain or will not provide the Chain Hook despite having Ichorised Chain, ensure you spoke to the correct Doll craftsman (Rakesh) and that you have the chain in your inventory. Behavior may vary by build.

- Tool exists but gap still blocked: The Chain Hook’s tooltip states it crosses pits, but a captured in-game clip of the crossing result is not present in the current footage. If you have the Chain Hook and cannot progress, record steps and report to official support or check later patch notes.

sections.title: Quick Answer
paragraphs: If you hit a gap or a corridor door with glowing “ghost-hands” (Open (A) prompt) and can’t go forward, turn around and go back to the foyer. At the rear of the foyer, next to the corridor/foyer transition, there is an unmarked vertical exit — a wooden rear stair / climb spot that shows Climb Up (A) / Climb Down (A). sections.title: What the stuck state looks like
paragraphs: - Common presentation: an apparent dead‑end in the first‑floor corridor with either a visible gap in the floor/route or a door that displays glowing hands and an Open (A) prompt.

sections.title: Exact steps back to the foyer rear exit
paragraphs:
Follow these steps in order:
1. Stop trying to force the blocked door or push past the gap. Turn and walk back the way you came down the corridor toward the foyer.
2. Enter the foyer and move to the rear edge of that room where the corridor meets the foyer (the area shown in the footage as the foyer/corridor transition).
3. Look for a vertical transit prompt at the rear of the foyer — the game shows Climb Up (A) or Climb Down (A) when you’re in the correct spot.  
  
4. Use the Climb Up (A) prompt (or Climb Down if you need to go lower) to take the wooden rear stairs / climb exit. The wooden rear stairs are visually present at the foyer rear; the mini‑map does not show a stair icon for this exit.

sections.title: Common failure modes
paragraphs:
- Searching farther forward down the blocked corridor instead of backtracking — players repeatedly try to find a forward path and miss the actual exit behind them.  
- Trusting the mini‑map to show every climb/stair — this rear vertical exit does not appear as a labeled stair icon on the in‑game mini‑map in observed footage.

sections.title: What happens next
paragraphs:
- After using the rear climb/stairs, the location banner in observed Early Access footage changes to Bellflower Occult Institute - Upper (when ascending). The vertical exit can be used both up and down (Climb Up / Climb Down prompts were visible in the footage).  
  
- Using the rear exit moves you out of the blocked first‑floor corridor and continues normal progression from the foyer vertical transit.

sections.title: If This Didn't Work
paragraphs: - I don’t see a Climb Up/Down prompt: move closer to the rear wall of the foyer where the corridor meets the room. The prompt only appears when you’re in the small climb/stairs interaction zone.
- Mini‑map shows the foyer but no stair icon: this is expected — the stair/climb exit is not marked on the in‑game mini‑map in observed footage. Do not rely on a map icon to find it.
- If you still can’t find it, backtrack fully to the foyer entrance and sweep the rear edge of the room where the corridor connects; the climb prompt is near that transition.

faq.question: Why doesn’t the mini‑map show the rear stairs or climb?
faq.answer: In Early Access footage the mini‑map displays the foyer geometry but does not mark this climb/stair as a labeled stair icon. The climb is visible in the world and appears as a Climb Up (A) / Climb Down (A) prompt when you stand in the interaction zone.

faq.question: Is this the Institute Code Words / basement door puzzle?
faq.answer: No. The blocked corridor (gap / ghost‑hands door) that requires returning to the foyer rear climb is a separate issue. The Institute Code Words and basement‑door puzzles are distinct and are covered by their own guides.

sections.title: Arm talismans — confirmed role only
paragraphs: - Role (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL): Arm talismans attach to limb attacks and modify those attacks' behaviour. In Early Access they are confirmed to either increase damage or reduce resource consumption for affected attacks (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL).

sections.title: Body talismans — the four special slots
paragraphs: - Role (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL): Body talismans use one of four dedicated body slots. They provide defensive or support-style effects and, in some cases, can retrigger arm talisman effects when their conditions are met (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL).

sections.title: Patch 0.36 — named The Freak classifications and Four Eyes fix
paragraphs:
CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL — 0.36 (released 2026-09-09) included the following named changes for The Freak talismans:
- Enchanted Candelabrum secondary = Spell (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL)  
- Spectral Blade attacks = Spell (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL)  
- Spectral Claws primary = Melee (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL)  
- Initiate's Candlestick = Spell (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL)
Also in 0.36: Fixed magic-toll talismans such as Four Eyes occasionally miscounting (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL).

Do not assume additional The Freak entries or other attack-class assignments beyond the four lines above; this section lists only the confirmed 0.36 named classifications and the Four Eyes miscount fix (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL).

paragraphs:

- Catalog note: This page is a system overview, not a tier list, and does not attempt a wholesale catalog. Verified talisman entries will be added incrementally.

sections.title: Four Arms + Birdcage — player reports (PLAYER_REPORTED)
paragraphs:
- PLAYER_REPORTED: Community reports indicate equipping the Four Arms body talisman may generate an extra counted hit in the Birdcage / B2 hanging-target puzzle. One player reported that incorrect responses stopped after unequipping Four Arms (PLAYER_REPORTED).  
- Do not treat these reports as an official bug confirmation or an official fix. For the puzzle’s expected inputs and rules, consult the Birdcage guide: /birdcage-b2-puzzle/ (PLAYER_REPORTED).

paragraphs:
- Incremental additions: individual, verified talisman entries will be added one at a time with source notes and an evidence grade.

- No tier lists: this page will not publish S/A/B-style rankings. It will present verified descriptions and use-cases so entries remain comparable without speculative ranking.

sections.title: If this didn't work / verification steps
paragraphs:
If you experience a Birdcage / B2 discrepancy and want to test whether a body talisman is involved (PLAYER_REPORTED):
1. Record your current talisman setup (screenshot or video) so you can restore it.  
2. Unequip suspect body talismans (for example, Four Arms as reported) and retry the Birdcage / B2 sequence.  
3. If the puzzle behaves differently after unequipping, document the exact steps and any reproducible pattern; community reports like this are useful to other players and to official support. (PLAYER_REPORTED)  
4. Consult /birdcage-b2-puzzle/ for the expected input sequence before testing to avoid conflating input errors with talisman effects.
Note: these are practical verification suggestions based on PLAYER_REPORTED accounts and do not replace official developer confirmation.

sections.title: FAQ
paragraphs:
Q: Are arm talismans the same as body talismans?
A: No. Arm talismans modify attacks (they can boost damage or reduce resource use) while body talismans occupy one of four special slots that provide protection or can retrigger arm talisman effects (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL).

Q: How many talismans are in Early Access?
A: The Early Access build contains 70+ talismans (CONFIRMED_OFFICIAL). The catalog on this page is incomplete and will expand as entries are verified.

A: No. This page explains system roles and behaviour and will add verified talisman entries incrementally. It will not publish tier rankings.

Q: Does Four Arms break the Birdcage puzzle?
A: There are PLAYER_REPORTED accounts that Four Arms can cause an extra counted hit or incorrect responses in the Birdcage / B2 hanging-target puzzle; one player reported the issue stopped after unequipping Four Arms. These are community reports and not an official bug confirmation. See /birdcage-b2-puzzle/ for the puzzle rule set. (PLAYER_REPORTED)

Exploration implications (practical, provisional)
Follow these steps when you plan a night revisit:

1. Prepare: stock healing items and any consumables you normally rely on. Expect encounters you did not see during daytime.
2. Prioritize safety outside Penwyll: official framing indicates higher danger outside Penwyll, so move cautiously in open areas beyond Penwyll limits.
3. Look for new content: inspect areas you previously cleared for hidden interactions or changed geometry — new creatures and secrets have been reported in official framing.
4. Avoid unverified guides: do not adopt community “night-route” tables as fact until they are confirmed; treating them as tentative reduces wasted time.
5. Record evidence: if you find what appears to be a night-only creature or secret, capture video or screenshots with timestamps and the current patch noted (see verification block below).

If this didn't work — how to verify & report
1. Check the official patch notes and the game's official channels first (note the latest observed patch page: 0.34 and research checked on 2026-09-07).
2. Reproduce your observation on the same patch version. If you can reproduce it reliably, capture short video (include location name and in-game indicators if available).
3. When reporting, include: exact location name, what changed at night, patch version, timestamp, and your reproduction steps. Attach media.
4. Submit via the developer’s official reporting channels or community verification threads so the observation can be verified before it becomes a published route or list.

Common mistakes
- Treating unverified community “night-route” tables as authoritative.
- Assuming night is uniformly harder inside every interior of Penwyll.
- Publishing named night-only lists or farming routes before developer confirmation.
- Forgetting to note the patch version or timestamp when reporting sightings.

- Keep an eye on official patch notes (patch observed: 0.34 at research check 2026-09-07) for changes that alter night behavior or balance.
